cards.title: Patch format specification
cards.description: Versioned JSON Schema of a patch (boxes, cables, parameters): the contract shared by the engine, the SDKs, the editor, the AI assistant and MCP. Published with its reference documentation.

tasks.title: Version 1: boxes, parameters and cables (spec/patch-format.md, read by engine-patch)
JSON Schema of the format, published with its reference documentation
Box arguments (ports computed at creation, e.g. multichannel output) and the project's own box naming conventions
Coverage-guided fuzzing of patch reading (cargo-fuzz, a versioned corpus seeded from the conformance cases), then native-versus-WebAssembly differential runs of the same inputs

Collaboration-ready identities (format version 2): box and cable identifiers unique across documents and stable for their life, generated by any client without coordination (128-bit, such as UUIDv7 or ULID, never a counter), still giving a total, deterministic order where the format orders by identifier; a documented migration from version 1's integers

Merge-friendly ordered lists: the explicit order of an outlet's cables (and any other ordered list) stored as sortable position keys (fractional indexing, ties broken by identifier), so concurrent insertions by two people merge without conflict; a document stays valid after any merge, and what it means (a cycle, a layout mismatch) is checked when the plan is built, like any patch

cards.title: Public API of the engine library, in Rust, C and TypeScript
cards.description: The engine's public interface, designed in one place and grown with each step of #12 that adds a piece of it: a low-level host API, the box contract, a toolkit of proven DSP building blocks, and a patch builder; exposed in Rust, through a C interface (functions written in Rust with the C calling convention, the bridge every other language can call), and in TypeScript over the WebAssembly module. Other languages come with the work that needs them. Stabilized and versioned by #29.

tasks.title: An API specification in spec/, completed at each step of #12 that adds a piece (host settings, events, the return path, state, hot swap, the box contract)
Low-level host API in Rust: build a plan from a graph, process blocks, send timestamped events, read the return path, save and restore state, swap plans; no_std, no allocation while processing
The box contract, versioned: what a box implements (inputs, outputs, events, state, latency, its modes), usable by built-in boxes and third-party externals

A DSP toolkit crate (engine-dsp): proven building blocks (oscillators, filters stable under modulation, smoothers, delay lines, interpolation, oversampling, envelopes, the deterministic FFT) and the math layer; the boxes are built with it
A patch builder in Rust: assemble boxes and cables in code, without writing a document
The C interface, written in Rust (extern "C"), with its header; the existing WebAssembly interface becomes one case of it; isolated, audited unsafe, checked by Miri
TypeScript over the WebAssembly module, the same functions as the C interface
Every interface checked against the same test vectors and conformance hashes, a gate proving the Rust, C and TypeScript surfaces expose the same functions
Examples that run as tests: a native host, a page in the browser, writing a box, building a patch in code
Further languages when their work needs them (Swift and Kotlin with the mobile exports, C# for game engines, Python for research), each a thin layer over the C interface, checked on the same vectors
A C interface with handles and no lock: several engines at once, never blocking the audio thread (then a WebAssembly build with threads can be allowed)

Typed errors end to end: each operation returns only the errors it can raise (SampleRate::new, Renderer::render); error codes in the C library, exported error classes in TypeScript, each class named by the API importable through the package name and recognized by instanceof; distinct load errors (bytes that are not UTF-8, an unsupported rate, an invalid patch, a plan that cannot be built); the cause of a failure on the audio thread kept as a field of its own
One patch loader shared by native and WebAssembly, with a differential test
The public API tracked by cargo public-api: no change goes unnoticed
Final names of the public engine API, with a glossary; a Node entry point for the npm package; the Rust render hash takes a checked render, its channel count proven to match its samples
Box registries valid by construction: a registry from outside the engine is checked (unique names, complete metadata, finite ranges) before any plan uses it

Every native entry point that does float work (building, processing, rendering, the C functions) takes the DefaultMode proof of engine-fpenv or opens its scope itself, so that a native call outside the processor's default floating-point mode does not compile: a proof engine-core's entry points take, or a native layer over them as the one boundary a native host uses, decided here

cards.title: First version of the patch editor
cards.description: A first web editor for patches, built on the patch format (#3): place boxes, connect them with cables, edit their parameters, play the patch with the engine, save and load the document. Every edit is a tested command with undo and redo; the interface follows the project's interface test strategy from its first line.

tasks.title: Patch model and command layer: every edit a command (add, remove, move, connect, disconnect, set parameter), each tested for success, rejection and undo/redo round trip, with property tests over random command sequences
Load and save documents in the patch format of #3, the serialization round trip identical
Canvas: boxes and cables drawn, selected, moved and connected with mouse, touch and keyboard; zoom and pan
Box creation by typing its name, with the registry's boxes and their parameters
Message cables and their explicit order on an outlet, shown when an outlet feeds several inlets, reorderable
Play and stop the patch with the engine in the browser, a running patch updated live as it is edited
Accessibility audited in every state, end-to-end tests on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, visual regression (#14)

cards.title: Publish the engine as an open-source library
cards.description: Once roadmap #12 is closed, the audio engine (core, boxes, DSP toolkit, WebAssembly binding) is published as an open-source library with its proofs (conformance, independent oracle, gates, CI), so that Rust, web and other developers can use it on its own; daily work stays in the monorepo, and the application uses the engine through its public API like any other user.

tasks.title: License chosen by the maintainer

Make the engine publishable from the monorepo: its crates and packages build and pass their proofs on their own; optionally a read-only mirror repository for the library (published by CI, outside contributions imported back into the monorepo)
Stabilize the public API: entry points, host settings, events, the box contract, versioned
External documentation and examples (native host, WebAssembly in the browser, writing a box)
Publish the crates on crates.io and the WebAssembly package
The application depends on the published engine

Demos of the library on the public website (#4): every box heard and checked in the browser (live controls, scope and spectrum, its measurements and thresholds, its reference hash recomputed on the page, code examples); sound sources generated by patches by default, the user's microphone or file, and a small bank of licensed recordings kept out of git (a manifest with SHA-256 in git, files published with the site and verified on load)

cards.description: Organize the repository as separate parts with clear contracts: the patch format spec, the reusable engine core, thin developer SDKs, the applications and the conformance corpus.

Placeholder folders with a README each (spec, bindings, apps, conformance)
Move the roadmap to apps/roadmap
Root pnpm workspace (shared configs extracted later, when a second package needs them)
xtask, pre-push hook and CI updated for the new layout

cards.title: Debug mode: JavaScript API to observe and drive the engine
cards.description: Enabled with ?debug in the web apps: one JavaScript API for people, AI agents driving a browser and the end-to-end tests, read-only on the audio side.

tasks.title: First version in the playground: help, snapshot, signal, levels, pitch, renderOffline
Readable text in the page for every measurement, plus debug.help()
Used by the playground end-to-end tests on 4 browsers
Documented, 100% coverage and mutation testing
Pitch estimator valid across the whole audio band, replacing zero crossings
Levels: sample peak and true peak, in dBFS

Oscilloscope: window in seconds at every rate, reduced motion honoured, no allocation per frame by construction (caller-owned buffers: no copy of the history per frame, one zero-crossing pass instead of two, no point object per sample, no spread when drawing, min/max decimation above one sample per device pixel; drawScope given the same buffers on consecutive frames, tested; an ESLint rule banning allocation in frame functions), redrawn when resized while stopped, and an accessible hint of what to do while nothing plays

Slow motion for debugging logic: the editor drives the engine as an offline host, at a chosen speed (from real time down to a few frames per second) or frame by frame, at 48 kHz unchanged, so what is seen slowed is bit for bit what runs at full speed
Step to the next frame, the next event or the next message; breakpoints on a message reaching a box, a value crossing a threshold, or a frame
Messages animated along their cables in their exact delivery order (the explicit order of an outlet's cables visible), with every box's values, from the engine's trace stream
Rewind: go back to an earlier frame through state snapshots and the seek law; replay a live session from its event log, slowed, up to the moment of a problem

cards.title: Reduce the size of the WebAssembly engine
cards.description: The proof of concept weighs 290 KB, largely the JSON reader (serde_json). Measure what each part costs, then shrink it (a lighter patch reader, wasm-opt, size-oriented build profile) without changing a single output sample: the conformance hashes must stay identical.

tasks.title: Measure the size of each part of the module
A lighter patch reader
A size budget, and a committed digest of the module with a command to update it, both checked by cargo xtask check on every machine
Compile the module once and pass it to the worklet, checked on every browser
Size-oriented build profile and wasm-opt, once the benchmarks of #12 exist

cards.title: Visual regression tests for the web interfaces
cards.description: Screenshots of the playground, the roadmap and later the editor, compared on every browser in a pinned rendering environment, so that a visual change is always seen and approved.

cards.title: Mutation testing of Astro templates

Rename everywhere: crates, packages, roadmap, docs, CI, and the history
Check that no trace of the working name remains before the first publication

cards.title: Declare the supported browsers
cards.description: Name the oldest version of each browser the playground, the editor and the documentation site support, and check the code against that baseline (a lint of the web APIs used, or a build target), so that an older browser always gets the explanation of what it lacks, never a TypeError. Until then, newer APIs are banned one by one by the shared lint configuration.

cards.title: Mobile browsers: live playground checks on iOS Safari and Android Chrome
cards.description: Check on real phones what desktop engines and emulators cannot show: interruptions, the silent switch, resuming and fades, with a written protocol and automated checks where a device can be driven.

tasks.title: A written protocol for checks on real devices (models, OS and browser versions, what to listen for), and a record of each run
Interruptions on iOS and Android: a phone call, a voice assistant, another app playing, Safari's "interrupted" state; the page shows the truth and resuming fades in without a click
The iPhone silent switch: sound is heard, or the page says why; navigator.audioSession set to playback where supported, feature-detected and tested
A Resume the browser refuses, and its message, seen on a device
Automated where a device can be driven (simulators or a device farm); otherwise listed as reviewed in the published known deviations
Start the playground while an interruption is already active (during a phone call): the page says why there is no sound, and starts once the call ends

cards.title: Split xtask into modules
cards.description: The project automation is one library file of about two thousand lines, with its tests in one file as long. Split it into modules by concern (the runner, the gates, the steps, the command line), each with its own tests, without changing a step, a message or a verdict. Do it together with the next new gate, so that the reviewed lists of unviable mutants, keyed by file, move once.

cards.title: macOS CI job: native aarch64 conformance and Safari
cards.description: CI runs on one x86_64 Linux runner: native conformance on aarch64 is proven only by the pre-push check of a Mac, and the browser tests run WebKitGTK, not Safari. Add a macOS job that renders the conformance corpus natively on aarch64 and in Safari and compares every hash with the committed references, once the repository is public or the first box heavy in floating point lands.

cards.title: Audit the CI workflow with zizmor
cards.description: The workflow gate of cargo xtask check reads the CI workflow with a strict line grammar written for this project. A dedicated workflow auditor such as zizmor would also catch the classes of mistakes the grammar does not know. Decide whether to adopt it as a pinned tool, record it in the dependency register, and run it from cargo xtask check.

cards.title: First CI run follow-up
cards.description: The CI workflow has not completed a run yet, so what it proves, how long it takes and how it behaves on GitHub are still assumptions. Run it once, measure it, and check on GitHub the behaviors that only GitHub can show.

tasks.title: Run the full workflow once and record its duration, the number of mutants tested and whether the caches were reused
Set each job's timeout-minutes to 1.5 times the measured duration of its part
Check live audio in Firefox and WebKitGTK on a runner without a sound card
Open a no-op pull request and check that the history gate passes on GitHub's merge ref
Check that the concurrency group of a skipped run does not cancel a requested run in progress
Split the full check into parallel jobs (parts and mutation shards from xtask, proven to cover every step once)

cards.title: Hardening from the third review
cards.description: The third review found small defects across the engine, the bindings, the tools, the tests, the pages and the documentation that no current card covers. Each step names a defect and its fix; take them by area, next to related work when a card already touches the same files.

tasks.title: Patch reading: the format version is checked after the whole document parses, so a version-2 patch is reported as an unknown field; read format first. engine-cli and the oracle skip non-.json entries of cases/ and patches/ silently; refuse them

Non-finite samples: cable and output sums keep NaN bits that depend on the target and on the build (the compiler may swap the operands of an addition); canonicalize NaN or refuse non-finite output, with a NaN-emitting test box, and reword the render-hash and patch-format specs to match. If sums keep NaN, the reduction tests that run in WebAssembly accept any quiet NaN there (its specification), never natively

Patch format spec: say how output boxes form the channels and in which order several are summed onto one channel, and that parameter ranges apply to the binary32 value; add a case with three output boxes and two range tests
Render hash: the three implementations accept different domains (rates, half frames) and Rendered has public fields; align the domains, add invalid vectors, make the fields private

Public types before the SDKs: port indices and case frames are pointer-wide (use u16 and u32), REGISTRY's type holds the box count (use a slice), wav_file pairs a header with any samples, and test-only items are pub (make them pub(crate))

osc~: the 440 Hz default is retyped as a fallback instead of derived from its parameter table; the phase wrap is never tested at an increment just below 1 or at whole cycles per sample; keep one render helper and one crossing counter; compute the 750 blocks of the comment, drop the redundant test, assert the zero-output call

osc~ wording: "identical on every target" lacks the flush-to-zero caveat, "at any frequency" should be "at any accepted frequency", and the derivations misstate the subnormal threshold, the rounding sequence and 0.999; reword the oracle and the box alike

Frame limits: the 2^29-frame domain does not hold end to end (the WAV header refuses stereo above 536,870,905 frames, even without --wav; the oracle cannot read 2 GiB files); state and enforce a frames times channels limit with boundary cases; render --wav and export also hold the samples twice, up to 8 GiB: stream the WAV, or document the peak

references.json: a duplicate key is accepted (the last wins) and hash shapes are not validated; refuse both. Reference hashes change "only through cargo xtask bless" is prose: require a reason in commits that touch the file, and drop "only"
engine_input trusts its caller for the patch size, so memory grows to any length; return null above the patch-size limit
safe_message escapes neither the backslash nor invisible format characters, and allocates a String per character; escape them and write in place

Wasm block copies: whole blocks are copied in host byte order and partial ones little-endian through a JS number, which canonicalizes NaN; assert little-endian at create and copy bits through a Uint32Array

Browser capture: the live subset is a hard-coded list and browser audio threads may flush subnormals; derive the subset from a case field, run the subnormal case live, and state that graph mixing may turn -0 into +0 at the capture point (or capture at the processor output)

Building the wasm views once at construction instead of on every block (an interface version bump), done with DSP foundations step 1; bless the two aliased 8 kHz sine cases at the same time, since the Nyquist policy moves them

Wasm errors: out of memory blames the module, a stack-overflow RangeError passes as a rate error, onprocessorerror drops the ErrorEvent detail, the worklet prints the cause twice, and #next repeats guarded's trap conversion; map each error precisely and reuse guarded

Tap messages: missing or short tap channels are filled with silence and tap does not validate its channel count; refuse them as malformed with capture's check. The public MarkedEngineNode.create contradicts its doc: make the doc true or the method private

Wasm scripts: they print stack traces and throw inside an error listener; wrap errors in BuildError and reuse guardStreams. The test server's decisions sit in an entry point no test runs, read errors become a silent 404, EADDRINUSE crashes with a stack, it listens on localhost while the README says 127.0.0.1, and HOME=/ breaks the path-leak scan; move it into a tested serveMain and fix each

Allocation tests: the garbage-collection count has no calibrated positive control and fewer quanta run at large sizes; use equal quanta, a small semi-space and a control that allocates one object per quantum
Oracle sine budget: the a times 2^-48 evaluation budget has no derivation and is 93% used, and no test starts at a non-zero phase; write the budget and its preconditions, and test a phase near 2 pi

Roadmap board file: it is written in place (write a temporary file, then rename); parseBoard trims texts so validate passes a board the next command rewrites (refuse untrimmed text, compare with the serialization); keys are compared joined (compare as sets); step numbers and positions are unbounded and 007 is accepted; year 0000 and createdAt after updatedAt pass; the page imports board.json through the JSON plugin (parse it with JSON.parse)

Roadmap CLI: positions count from 0 and steps from 1 (make both 1-based); HELP is typed apart from its tables and the move usage omits --position (build it from the tables); editCard re-implements updateCard; emptyBoard is a test-only export
Test ports: freePort accepts any value of its variable and its tests depend on the host network; accept only an integer in 1-65535 and inject the listener

Skipped tests: the focus/skip selector misses deep chains, it["skip"], the {skip: true} option, .fails and test.fail; widen it with fixtures, and read the Vitest and Playwright reports against an allowlist of statuses so a skipped or expected-failure test fails the check
Test rules without a tool: ban vi.waitFor in unit tests, and add a lint rule that refuses an action button whose onClick does not ignore the repeated clicks of a double-click, each with a fixture

Commit messages: the commit-msg hook validates a different text from the one git records (the -v scissors, # lines with -m, trailing whitespace), [skip ci] and its variants are not refused, and the BREAKING-CHANGE footer is ignored; apply git's cleanup first and handle each
Pre-push: run the check in a detached worktree of the pushed commit instead of the working tree, and test an annotated release tag pushed through the real hook

Check runner: a closed stdout (piped to head) changes the exit code, waits on children have no bound and no progress output, and the tree gate does not name the file whose changes changed; route stdout, print the elapsed time, list each file

Workflow gate: raw lines are tested against a deny-list, so quoted keys, "if :", a misplaced if: failure(), shell: and defaults:, toolchain or flag variables in env, secrets[...] and job-level permissions all pass; compare the whole file with a generated text or a strict grammar, one fixture per probe

Supply chain: the gate trims indentation and ignores exclusions (release-age and cooldown excludes, the Dependabot split, .npmrc, deny.toml ignores); the dependency gate exempts any path dependency and ignores [patch] and npm: overrides; the legacy extensionless .cargo/config is not refused; refuse each

Pinned versions: pnpm is not checked against packageManager, @types/node is not tied to the Node floor, the target list is typed twice, and the README retypes the pinned tool versions; tie each to its source with a test. Decide and record the remaining hardening options (build-script bans, strict dependency builds, trust policy, pnpm's blockExoticSubdeps, a hardened CI runner such as harden-runner, repository rules, Dependabot for the pins)

Setup: the hooks are silently not installed with ignore-scripts (drop "|| true", add a preflight item for core.hooksPath), and the preflight refuses only Windows (allow macOS and Linux); mention the Linux system dependencies of the browsers (--with-deps)

Check speed, measured first: a clean before each of the 12 coverage measurements rebuilds the workspace 12 times (one target directory per crate), cargo mutants runs with --jobs 1 (measure 2 and 3), engine.wasm ships a 35.8 KB name section (strip it), and the hash is updated once per sample (chunk it)

Gate parsers: compare_reviews splits at the first " -- ", mutant_key does not parse line and column, an empty Stryker mutator name is accepted, changelog dates are checked for shape only, the README gate matches a prefix, crate_root misses tests/<dir>/main.rs, benches, examples and src/bin, and coverage_locality matches a summary wording; fix each with a test

Hermetic tests: the hooks test has a hard-coded PATH and no GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, the list of local git variables misses one of git rev-parse --local-env-vars, and tests use predictable shared temporary paths with no cleanup on failure; one hermetic helper asserted against git's list, and CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR with a drop guard

Vocabulary gate: it skips .json, .astro, .txt and .toml, where British spellings and the old word for boxes have slipped in; "connection" is used for "cable"; digits are grouped three ways; nothing enforces the bans on other software names and the old project name; extend the gate and fix the occurrences
GLOSSARY gate: resolve every backticked Type::member name in GLOSSARY.md against the code, so a removed method fails the check

TypeScript @throws: the rule that @throws names the errors has no tool and many parsers have no tag; enable jsdoc/require-throws with a fixture. "Each lint rule is proven" covers only the policy's own rules: narrow the claim or snapshot the resolved configuration

Test assertions: error assertions are weak where the exact message is known, some tests take expected values from the module under test, the generator-check thresholds are retyped (512) with another strategy than the laws', the plan test boxes are copied and drifting, the scope has two constants for one interpolation error, and a spy on Promise.prototype.catch tests the implementation; assert exact literals, compute, share

Shared browser test helpers: the CSP probe is written three times, the contrast and Tab helpers twice (disagreeing on WebKit Tab, and one reads a translucent color as opaque), and three matrix readers drift; move them to @poyetik/config with a findUp, and add one axe helper that also fails on incomplete results, used by the roadmap and wasm suites

Playwright projects: the WebKit and mobile WebKit projects use default time zone and locale, so their emulation cannot be seen to work; give each a non-default value. The roadmap config does not set workers like the others, and fixed preview ports remain; share the settings

Playground failure paths: a failure while playing cuts the sound with no fade; the fade-out starts from a stale gain value read on the main thread; a second refused Resume re-renders nothing; Details shows String(error) without the cause; a failed body download does not name the URL; fix each with a test

Playground in a real browser: the mute query sets the gain to 0 and the fake AudioParam jumps to its target, so cancel, unsupported, refused resume, failures, stopping and the fades are never observed; mute after the gain stage, make the fake ramp, add the e2e tests, and assert the text and computed styles of the sizer and the disabled button

Playground styles: the unsupported button shows a wait cursor and a hover accent (use not-allowed, no hover on aria-disabled), hover sticks on touch screens (@media (hover: hover)), the Details summary keeps the default focus ring and its keyboard path is untested, the peak has no unit (dBFS) and the frequency dash is unexplained

Playground single sources: 440 Hz and the theme colors are typed twice, the played patch is a retyped copy of a corpus file compared after parsing (import its bytes), states are compared by identity and by kind, a local window shadows the global, a history of size 0 gives NaN indices, and a throwing scope frame stops silently with no error boundary
Scope frequency: frequency() is off by up to 0.124 Hz on short inputs inside its domain, and its derivation is wrong; add a derived minimum span (about 4 ms), fix the comment, test the worst case

Roadmap page order: between 561 and 900 px In progress sits below the backlog, on a phone Later comes before Next, and order: -1 makes the visual order differ from the reading and focus order; one narrow-screen rule keeping the DOM order, e2e at 390 and 700 px comparing visual and Tab order; the aria-labels Progress and Steps are untested, and "Steps 1/3" may be read as a fraction or a date: assert the names and say "1 of 3"

Documentation claims: numbers retyped in comments and specs with no test (name or compute them), the bypass register "holds only" entries but holds a test helper, README commands no check runs (a smoke run or a narrower rule), the README spec row omits the render hash, the crates README undersells engine-testkit, and the GLOSSARY rows of render hash and conformance case are incomplete

Consistent naming: case names (sine-<hz>-at-<rate> through bless), keys of one concept across formats (with the patch format card), EngineTrap without the Error suffix and name set two ways (with the SDK card), the project name's capitalization, the quoting of names in messages, module header comments, and the two checkers' verdict words with a missing-reference hint naming cargo xtask bless
Conformance spec: a spec/ page for the formats of the conformance files (cases, expectations, references), which the four readers then follow
Oracle: refuse duplicate keys in case files, as engine-cli does
Browser test harness: accept only the engine's sample rate range in case files
engine-cli: open inputs with a bound and refuse anything but a regular file, so a FIFO cannot block a read
engine-wasm: a capture on a context that never runs, or on a source that never produces input, still waits forever: race it against the context's state and the engine's failure
Playground: an end-to-end test that starts the player from an already suspended context in every browser project (today checked once by hand; Safari unchecked)
xtask: test its copy of the safe-message escaping against spec/safe-message-vectors.json, as engine-patch and the TypeScript tools do
xtask: a test that every command it runs gets no input (stdin closed)
xtask: match stryker case-insensitively in the package-script gate
xtask: the 1,000-character cap cuts long legitimate detail lines and escapes the colors of a failed command's captured stderr: bound only quoted untrusted values
engine-wasm: renderOffline reports a late rejected or failed message as started too late or engine stopped: keep the real cause, with a test of that order
engine-wasm: prove in a real browser that a stopped engine gives the tap an empty input (the source-stopped signal is tested with fakes only)
Playground: the interleaving test that mocks the loader is trivially true; make it vary the mocked load latency
Oracle: refuse a missing pad byte after any odd-sized WAV chunk, not only the last
xtask bypass gate: a comment inside an attribute (#[/* x */ignore]) is not caught; tokenize instead of matching text
A gate refusing heavy binary files in git (audio files, files above a size limit) unless reviewed; demos store patches, never rendered sound

Measurement floor proof: bounds_its_own_error_by_the_floor adds one coefficient's error per sample, but up to 22 fitted coefficients sum per sample and a spur reading can double it, which gives about 1.5e-11 for the spur floor against 2^-36 (1.455e-11); redo the derivation term by term and fix the floor or its proof

Measurement spec: say that the bound checks derived from the error per sample mainly test the measurement code, and that only the checks against a predicted level (such as the THD+N of binary32 rounding) can catch a defect of the box measured

Oracle measurements: measure.ts follows the Rust algorithm almost line for line, so it proves an independent implementation, not an independent algorithm; add a cross-check that computes the levels another way (for example from the windowed spectrum) and say which kind of independence each check gives

Browser tests on the developer's machine: the Firefox and WebKit end-to-end tests open the real sound card and disturb audio playing in other browsers; give them a silent output or a fake audio device locally, with a test that proves the emulation is in force

Mutation timeouts: the default check sets the mutant timeout automatically (about 40 s for xtask's main.rs), and one mutant timed out under load although more time caught it; set a timeout derived from the measured baseline with a margin, or rerun timed-out mutants once with more time

Benchmark baseline: its update path (cargo xtask bless-benchmarks) is a convention, not a gate: a hand edit of spec/benchmark-baseline.json passes, as one of conformance/references.json does; require the bless or a reason in commits that touch it

Benchmark n log n law: it has little room at the measured sizes, since loading is dominated by linear parsing (a quadratic term must reach about 6% of the linear cost from 4096 to 16384 boxes before failing); add a size or a law that isolates plan building
Plan benchmarks: the measured patches are bipartite, so the depth handling of the execution-order sort is not exercised; add a deep topology once a box has both inlets and outlets
Wasm instrumenter: it reads the value types of locals and typed selects as one byte; refuse explicitly any type byte other than 0x7f to 0x7b, 0x70 and 0x6f, with a fixture
Construction timing harness: node.disconnect() leaves the 20 timed processors alive in one context; end each processor (or use a fresh context) so later runs do not share its load
Browser construction bounds: measured on the maintainer's Mac only, unconfirmed on the CI runner; measure on CI and record where

Native float mode, host side: decision 11 also has native shells detect, in safe code, a floating-point mode they could not set and report it; engine-fpenv always sets it on x86_64 and aarch64, so nothing reports yet. Implement the detection and report with the first plugin shell (with a mode that foreign code changes inside an engine call, which with_default_mode undoes on exit but whose proof is false until then), or scope it in the spec there

Native float mode inside a call: when the host is already in the default mode, with_default_mode writes nothing on entry, so a mode change made by foreign code inside its body is not undone on exit; document the precondition where engine calls reach foreign code, or always restore the mode found on entry

MXCSR bit 17 (MM, the misaligned exception mask of some AMD processors) is outside the mode fields of engine-fpenv and kept as the host set it: confirm on an AMD runner that it cannot change a result, and say so in the audit
Browser render hash: renderHash (bindings/wasm) defaults the arithmetic mode to 0n with nothing tying it to the module's MODE; export the module's mode and hash with it once a second mode exists
Unknown arithmetic mode: the oracle, engine-hash and the browser renderHash word their refusal differently; one message and a shared vector of it

Math layer gate: it sees only a direct libm dependency of a box crate; also refuse engine-testkit as a normal dependency of a box crate, and math reached through other crates (num-traits, a libm feature of another dependency)
Box laws: parameters are tried only at binary32-representable values; extend them to binary64 values with patch format version 2

Binary32 error bound of a gain: when a box multiplies by a gain not exact in binary32, rounded through from_binary64 before the product, its bound counts one more 2^(e-25); state it in the shared formula when the first gain box lands
Math layer gate: decide whether casts to an inferred type (as _) given to Binary64::new are refused by the gate rather than left to review and to the as_conversions lint
Math layer gate: read every file box code compiles (include!d files, #[path] modules outside src/, a future build.rs) or refuse them in box crates

Decision 10's cost claim: the newtypes' instruction counts are held only within the benchmark tolerance; prove them identical to plain floats (an exact comparison of the counts) or keep the weaker wording

cards.title: Make the repository public
cards.description: Open the repository to everyone once its history and settings are ready: what a public repository shows and allows, decided before the switch.

tasks.title: Decide the author email of the history: keep it, or rewrite every commit to the GitHub noreply address before the switch (every SHA and the v0.1.0 tag change; force-push while the repository is still private), and set git to the chosen address for future commits
Re-audit the whole history just before the switch: no secret, no local-only file, no forbidden name
Keep the setting that requires approval before running workflows for first-time contributors, and check the workflow gives forked pull requests a read-only token and no secret
Decide what a public repository without a license means for contributors, or choose the license first (ticket #6)
Switch the visibility (maintainer's action or explicit approval)

cards.title: DSP foundations: state-of-the-art audio quality before more boxes
cards.description: Set the audio quality bar before writing many boxes: objective measurements, deterministic denormals, smoothed parameters with sample-accurate events, an allocation-free audio thread in the browser, and benchmarks.

tasks.title: Engine design decisions, recorded before any code that depends on them: messages, event scheduling, feedback, polyphony, multichannel, rates, parallelism, hot swap, latency, state; including the Nyquist policy of oscillators, an exact integer phase accumulator, the output stage (headroom, non-finite samples), the input domain of boxes, and compiling, instantiating, parsing and building plans off the audio thread, or bounding and measuring what must stay there (the construction of the engine processor), hot swap included

Objective measurements in engine-testkit and the oracle: spectrum, THD, SNR, aliasing level, with thresholds per box; spur and aliasing laws across the rate matrix; the banned float methods audited against the toolchain
Benchmarks in CI: instruction counts per box and for building large plans, with regression thresholds; the construction of the engine processor timed on the three browser engines
Deterministic strategy for denormal numbers, proven on every target: a subnormal conformance case, and a native test with flush-to-zero forced on
Subnormal parameters treated as zero (flushed on the f64 side before rounding, below the smallest normal), with the denormal strategy, and a 1e-40 Hz oscillator case

Engine precision: 64-bit processing by default and 32-bit as a setting, boxes written once, generic over the sample type, all their arithmetic through the engine's math layer (the sample type, its operators and the math functions); a render hash version that records the precision and the arithmetic mode as a versioned set of option flags (all off, the strict default, the only one built), an unknown flag refused; every reference re-blessed for both precisions (a migration step), checked native and WebAssembly

Reduction order: every sum of more than two terms through one helper, 16 lanes summed in order then a fixed pairwise tree, whatever the machine's SIMD width; tested against a literal scalar reference on every target (with step 6's re-bless)

Box algorithm versions: every box carries its algorithm version in the patch, any change of bits takes a new one, old versions keep playing or migrate explicitly (with step 6 and format version 2); then a deep review of this block (steps 6 to 8) on its pull request, with a green full check
Output stage: raw and protected (safety limiter) modes; non-finite samples always replaced and reported; the playground protected by default

Host settings: sample rate, host buffer, engine block and channel counts chosen by the host, renders independent of the engine block (reduced-rate updates only on a grid of absolute frames), settings a host cannot honor reported
Patches without audio output: time advances and every box runs with zero channels, in the native renderer as in the WebAssembly engine (today one runs no box, the other runs them all)

Execution modes: live, offline and build give the same bits; every box type declares itself live-capable or offline-only, the real-time rules proven on every live-capable box, and a live plan refusing an offline-only box

Box contract as a public, versioned ABI shared by built-in boxes and third-party externals: explicit state, compile-friendly processing, buffers aligned to 64 bytes and padded, routing resolved when the plan is built; every built-in box giving the same bits directly and through the ABI; instantaneous responses and sub-sample discontinuity ports declared

Typed, smoothed parameters (kinds such as frequency, with a declared Nyquist policy) and sample-accurate timestamped events, in the engine and the patch format; an event quantum per patch and subpatch (1 frame by default); a box reads its parameter values through a typed access that cannot be missing, so that no box keeps a fallback default of its own (osc~'s 440 Hz, #24 item 6)
Messages and rates: every parameter driven by messages or by an audio-rate signal; a total order of messages within a frame; MIDI input as timestamped events (MIDI 2.0 packets, MPE)

Message payloads: trigger, number, symbol, list, MIDI 2.0 packet, note with its spelling, resource; bounded and allocation-free, symbols interned when the plan is built, typed message ports, overflow refused and reported

Control boundary: events stamped by the host (immediate or scheduled), times from other bases converted to the nearest frame by exact integer arithmetic; quotas and horizons enforced on the sending side, identical live and offline; a return path that never waits (timestamped streams, latest-value slots, engine reports, gaps reported exactly); a live event log replaying bit for bit

Seeded randomness: the seed in the patch, per-box streams from stable box paths, a counter-based generator addressed by frame, exact conversion to floats, a live new-seed mode that logs its seed; its laws; then a deep review of this block (steps 9 to 18) on its pull request, with a green full check

Oscillators: an exact 64-bit integer phase accumulator; band-limited by default, with a raw variant per box; hard sync with sub-sample discontinuities. The sine's angle is reduced exactly before any rounding to binary32 (the quadrant from the top bits of the integer phase, the rest folded exactly), since today's binary32 osc~ rounds an unreduced angle (about 11 to 13 dB of THD+N lost, a DC offset at a quarter and half the sample rate): osc~'s binary32 thresholds and predicted THD+N tightened to match, the prediction computed from the actual angles, with a test that a quarter of the sample rate gives exactly 0, 1, 0, -1
Long-run drift check of oscillators against the exact phase, skipping ahead in state to cover hours of signal

Allocation-free audio thread in the browser, without per-frame garbage: oscilloscope through an AnalyserNode; capture and metering through a SharedArrayBuffer ring when cross-origin isolated, with a tested fallback otherwise; garbage collections while rendering measured in every browser engine, not only in V8. Until then, the tap processor behind capture and the playground oscilloscope copies every render quantum on the audio thread (a known deviation, pinned by an allocation test)

Real-time cost: estimate a patch's cost per block before it runs and report its load, so that a valid patch too heavy for real time is flagged (after the benchmarks); measure the copy of every outlet into the bus each block and remove it if it costs
Silence skipping: a box declares when its output stays exactly zero, the engine skips it only then; a law that renders are identical with skipping on and off

Multichannel cables with automatic expansion and channel layouts (speaker roles and positions, ambisonic components, binaural, discrete; presets and custom layouts) checked when the plan is built; buses (sends, groups) summed in a fixed order
Deterministic FFT: one code path on every target, no run-time feature detection, twiddles from the pure-Rust libm, its error bounded against a higher-precision direct transform

Subpatches with their own block size, resampling and overlap, a block of 1 frame included; feedback cycles through an explicit delay, single-sample feedback included; delay-free loops resolved per sample (linear exactly, non-linear with a fixed iteration count)
Latency declared by boxes and compensated automatically, events aligned with the compensated audio
Serializable box state (presets, project save): a render saved and restored continues with the same bits
Seek law: a render that jumps to a frame with every state restored, by snapshot or replay, equals from that frame a render played from the start
Hot swap: patch edits while playing without a dropout, state transferred by box identity, optional crossfade; plans built off the audio thread, in the browser in bounded slices

Resources: content-addressed by SHA-256, immutable, decoded and resampled off the audio thread with the same code on every target, swapped at a frame, read through handles whether in memory or streamed, underruns logged; then a deep review of this block (steps 19 to 31) on its pull request, with a green full check
Polyphony: voices per subpatch with allocation and stealing policies, MPE; polyphony through multichannel cables
Parallel graph scheduling natively, with renders identical whatever the thread count
Render-ahead hooks: future events, plan parts marked live or ahead, invalidation from a frame by restoring state; a render with render-ahead identical to one without

Musical time hook: per-sample transport position, tempo and time signature for boxes, tempo changes sample-accurate; transports as exact time maps (tempo curves, recorded beats, irregular and additive meters, grooves, several transports, unpulsed time)
Audio input boxes, fed by the host
External processor boxes for third-party plugins: declared latency, imposed block size, opaque state, marked non-deterministic and excluded from hash guarantees

Clean the specification and the documentation once the engine is complete: spec/ keeps what and why (decisions, rules, laws, formats, acceptance tests), without planning (the Step and Order lines, the implementation order, what is implemented when, a section named after the ticket); the documentation describes the finished engine; then a deep review of this block (steps 32 to 38) on its pull request, with a green full check

cards.title: Oscilloscope in the web page with an on/off button
cards.description: A 440 Hz sine wave generated by the Rust engine (WASM in an AudioWorklet), played in the web page with an on/off button and shown live on an oscilloscope.

tasks.title: Install the Rust toolchain
engine-core: Object contract, strong types, fixed block, plan build and run (no_std, forbid unsafe)
engine-objects + engine-testkit: osc~ (440 Hz sine) passing the generic laws
engine-hash + engine-cli: offline render, canonical hash, first conformance case sine-440
bindings/wasm (engine-wasm + AudioWorklet glue): same hashes as native, proven by end-to-end tests on 4 browsers (OfflineAudioContext) and in Node
apps/playground: on/off button and live oscilloscope, end-to-end tests on 4 browsers
xtask check wired into CI and the pre-push hook
Independent conformance oracle (TypeScript): rereads the WAV of every case, recomputes the hashes and checks the expected signal, in cargo xtask check
Deep review: every finding analyzed and applied, then a fresh review

cards.title: Public website: documentation, roadmap and playground
cards.description: One public site, hosted: guides, the API reference of every part (generated from docstrings), the box reference generated from the registry metadata, the patch format reference generated from the schema, the roadmap page and the playground. The HTTP security headers live in versioned configuration and are tested against what the host really serves.

tasks.title: Choose the host
Set frame-ancestors and the other security headers (Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, Permissions-Policy) in versioned configuration
Test the headers the host really serves, in a check that fails when one is missing or different
The roadmap page and the playground served by the site
The engine library's demos (#29): every box playable and checked in the browser

cards.title: First image: a square moving with the sound, identical on every target
cards.description: The visual counterpart of #1: a white square on black, its position driven by the phase of an audio oscillator, rendered by the engine natively and in WebAssembly and shown live in the playground. Small on purpose: it builds the whole proof chain for images (exact CPU reference, canonical image hash, conformance across targets, GPU within a measured threshold, browser tests, independent oracle) on which every visual box will then be checked.

tasks.title: Visual operator contract in the core and a square operator, with exact edge coverage (antialiasing)
Exact CPU reference renderer: no_std, no unsafe code, built for every target of the portability check
Canonical hash of an image sequence, specified in spec/ with known-answer vectors read by every implementation
Offline render in engine-cli and the first visual conformance case: the same hashes natively and in WebAssembly
Sound and image on one clock: the instant of each image tied to the audio frames by an exact rule, the square following the phase of an audio oscillator
GPU backend (wgpu, justified like every dependency): the same images within a measured threshold of the reference, checked in CI on a software GPU
Playground: the square moving live with the sound in WebGPU, end-to-end tests on the browsers
Independent oracle: rereads the images, recomputes the hashes and checks the motion
Wired into cargo xtask check
Deep review: every finding analyzed and applied, then a fresh review

cards.title: Visual foundations: design and quality bar of the visual engine before more boxes
cards.description: The visual counterpart of #12: decide the visual engine's design against the live-show targets, then set its quality and proof bar before writing many visual boxes. One core shared with the audio engine; other uses (editing, compositing, embedded) kept possible whenever it costs nothing.

tasks.title: Target matrix for the live show (node-based real-time visuals, lighting previsualization, media servers, LED pixel mapping and lasers, multi-machine shows): for each, the core concepts it needs; a target needing a new core concept is settled before any code

Engine design decisions, recorded before any code that depends on them: time and rates, push and pull computation, resources and GPU memory, data types (textures, buffers, geometry including vector paths, channels), colour pipeline, outputs, execution modes, random access, hot swap, latency, state; and interaction: the input event model (the image a gesture applies to), a scene queryable on the CPU for picking, the operator contract mapping output coordinates back to input coordinates, gesture-to-image latency, the state of interactive objects, 3D camera navigation and manipulators
The hooks of the shared core (time base, open port types) checked against the audio engine's decisions
Proof tiers declared per operator: exact (logic, CPU reference, integer GPU operations if proven), measured (floating-point GPU within derived thresholds), not guaranteed; shown by the editor
Shaders written once and translated for every GPU API; a deterministic CPU interpreter of the shader representation as the exact reference of any shader, user shaders included
Floating-point linear-light colour, with colour metadata (primaries, transfer, range) on every image
Objective image measurements in the test kit and the oracle (perceptual difference, colour difference, aliasing, banding), thresholds per operator with their derivation
Deterministic random access: rendering image n directly equals rendering from the start, stateful operators through checkpoints
Video input and output in the shells: decoded images with exact timestamps, colour and access cost; decoder conformance on a corpus of reference videos
Output stage: gamut and non-finite guard, and a flash limiter against photosensitive seizures
Four vertical slices on one core with no special case: raster on screen, vector paths to a simulated laser, an image mapped to DMX pixels over Art-Net, an offline render to a file
Benchmarks per operator in CI, quality tiers per device, a cost estimate warning when a patch will not keep up

Desktop editor shell chosen by a measured prototype on macOS, Windows and Linux (Tauri and Electron at least): the native GPU render shown inside the editor window without copying, low-latency native audio, the interface on each system's web engine; show outputs in separate native windows

Third-party visual operators in the editor: shaders validated by WebGPU, recovery from a lost GPU device without taking the editor down, GPU cost measured by timestamp queries, a determinism tier per shader (exact, measured, not guaranteed) with the CPU interpreter as reference, invariance to resolution and frame rate and random access in the compatibility report

Interaction with the output: pointer, multi-touch, pen, keyboard and gamepad inputs of every output window as timestamped events (recorded in the event log); coordinates converted through the render chain, projection-mapping warps inverted; exact picking (CPU ray casting in 3D, point-in-shape in 2D and vector); gesture-to-image latency measured; the base for interactive web pages and creative apps as build targets, and for the interface runtime of exported apps

Further capabilities weighed in the target matrix before the design decisions: a 3D scene shared with audio (sound sources, loudspeakers, lights and projectors as objects of one scene), keyframe animation and curves, cue states and crossfades between scenes, seeded fixed-timestep particles and simulations, physically based materials and lights in photometric units shared with the light previsualization, haze and fog, dynamic quality scaling live only and reported, asset import (glTF, SVG, point clouds, images, LUTs), surtitles and captions, camera and projector calibration, keying and masks, output recording, time remapping, visual debugging, headless rendering

cards.title: Third-party boxes in the editor: sandboxed WebAssembly externals with a compatibility report
cards.description: Let anyone write boxes, as WebAssembly modules implementing the public box contract, loaded in the editor (browser and desktop) without a server. The platform is protected by construction whatever an external does; its quality stays the author's, measured and shown; a compatibility report says which features it breaks and why. Exported apps stay fully compiled: externals are translated ahead of time and proven identical by conformance.

tasks.title: Box contract expressible across a WebAssembly boundary: a stable, versioned interface, the same for built-in boxes
Loading a module in the browser and desktop editor: contract check, requested capabilities shown and granted by the user, cached by content hash, referenced by content hash in patches
Platform protections, always on: a failing external goes silent and is reported, never the host; a memory ceiling; a deterministic cost budget counted by instructions injected at load

Static determinism analysis at load: relaxed SIMD, threads and shared memory, imports beyond the contract, reads of NaN bits; NaN canonicalization and identical stack and memory limits on every engine

Determinism declared by every box and propagated through the plan; each feature (collaboration, multi-machine, replay, seek and render-ahead, conformance hashes) declares what it requires and adapts or warns; non-deterministic outputs recorded in the event log like an audio input

Compatibility report computed in the browser without a server: static analysis at once, a quick test battery in Web Workers, a deeper one in the background, cached by content hash; each failed property mapped to the features it breaks; passes stated as measurements (cases run, code coverage)
Editor display: deterministic or not and why, labels (unverified, laws passed, verified, proven), cables downstream of a non-deterministic box marked
External SDK: a Rust crate and a C header, a project template, and an external check command producing the same report
Export: externals translated ahead of time, or compiled from source when they follow the engine's rules, proven identical to the WebAssembly version by conformance
Hot reload of our own boxes in development through the same mechanism
Catalogue: the full battery across WebAssembly engines, continuous fuzzing, reproducible builds proving a module comes from its published source
